questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I would like to go somewhere in Europe where I knew there would be a lot of culture opportunities and where the film culture was thriving. 
I wanted to explore a big city and go to a good university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, if you knew were to look and updated yourself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Newsletteres from the university, and the studentmail from home and away university. Also announcements that I could go to physically.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It went through the university, so it was easy in that sense. Just had to pay and be updated and they did it for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived far away from uni, maybe 8km, was a bit far out from the city which was a shame sometimes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really unlucky with the option I got, but that is just how it is.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I looked at the available courses on their webpage, I could easily see which ones I could take. Then I just selected the ones I wanted and it went on from there, vey easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were very quick to respond on email and very kind, so this was no problem.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, however I would have liked to be able to have more studies related to the subject I study at home and this was not so easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take time to look at them properly so you will have nice courses, it means more than you think to be motivated at the host university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 3 courses were very very nice and 2 of them kind of boring, but I picked them myself, so that is how it is.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had mostly second year bachelor courses on my exchange, which was perfectly fine for me on my BA. They were challenging and also interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very good in Amsterdam, very high level, very engaged students, the workload were also higher than UCPH and I learned a lot from their university. It was really hard just to pass, so they expected a lot from their students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
'Words, Sounds, Images: The Anthropology of Media'
'Body and Culture'
'Topic Algorithmic Persuasion in the Digital Society'
'Globalising cultures'
'Ancient Philosophy'

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would very much recommend Ancient philosophy, Body and culture and Words, Sounds, Images: The Anthropology of Media.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The first month was very expensive a lot of stuff for the apartment had to be bought, also just settling in always costs more than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: They were as expected, very similar to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were sports, and fitness, and social activities arranged for people to try out. I did in the beginning, parties and so on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hmm try the intro weeks out, otherwise I did not try anything else.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hang out with friends, visit museum and cinemas, learn about the history of the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was alright, there were a lot of other internationals which made it easier to make friends. And the culture was in general okay to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Just try, not everyone have time but there is always some at the University who also finds it interesting to meet internationals. 
Talk to them during breaks etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To find the nice places in the city, but ask locals instead of google, because otherwise you will just see the turist-things.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The lovely atmosphere in the city, the great culture offers for students visiting.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- do an effort to make some great friends, it will make your exchange way better. 
- explore the city, ask locals were to go, they know.
- save up for the exchange, it is expensive but not nice to go if you can't afford going out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The workload is high at UvA, so be ready for this, you have to prepare and know your stuff. 
Live in the city, I lived to far away which was not so nice.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The personal experience, I learned a lot going on my own and establish myself in another country. Making friends and do everything on my own initiative.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Also making good friends, it can be difficult with just one semester abroad.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
